radar.name: VisualTrust
radar.title: VisualTrust
radar.description: VisualTrust is a counterfactual video question-answering benchmark with 5,063 cases across 14 claim-fact classes, pairing each question with no-claim, accurate-claim, and misleading-claim versions of the same video.
radar.oneLine: VisualTrust is a counterfactual video question-answering benchmark with 5,063 cases across 14 claim-fact classes, pairing each question with no-claim, accurate-claim, and misleading-claim versions of the same video.
radar.forecastReason: The counterfactual video setup and large model comparison are topical, but artifact readiness and standalone evaluation paths are not clearly established.

radar.name: Visual Sanad
radar.title: Visual Sanad
radar.description: Visual Sanad is a controlled benchmark of 2,400 rendered images built from 100 English Qur'an verses, four factual states per verse, and six visual conditions, used to test whether vision-language models falsely accept incorrect Qur'anic verse attributions.
radar.oneLine: Visual Sanad is a controlled benchmark of 2,400 rendered images built from 100 English Qur'an verses, four factual states per verse, and six visual conditions, used to test whether vision-language models falsely accept incorrect Qur'anic verse attributions.

publication.venue: poster presentation at the Muslims in Machine Learning (MusIML) Workshop at NeurIPS 2026

radar.forecastReason: The domain is culturally specific and the artifact appears limited to a workshop paper snapshot, which constrains broad early attention.

radar.name: VALCON
radar.title: VALCON
radar.description: VALCON is a benchmark suite with three suites (VAB-Consistency, VAB-Boundary, VAB-Challenge) that pairs an LLM's generation of value-conditioned question-answer samples with its own judgments under the same value principles, scoring self-reflective consistency across roles.
radar.oneLine: VALCON is a benchmark suite with three suites (VAB-Consistency, VAB-Boundary, VAB-Challenge) that pairs an LLM's generation of value-conditioned question-answer samples with its own judgments under the same value principles, scoring self-reflective consistency across roles.

publication.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

radar.forecastReason: The suite covers a broad LLM alignment question with released bilingual data and code, which supports interest among alignment and evaluation researchers.
